claim: Standard data-parallel training moves 2Psi bytes per step, because all-reduce decomposes into a reduce-scatter and an all-gather that each move Psi elements.
stance_target: the baseline against which FSDP/ZeRO communication multipliers are computed
scope_conditions: Bandwidth-bound regime; large model where latency is negligible; ring/pipelined collectives
quoted_support: Both reduce-scatter and all-gather are implemented using a pipelined approach, that results in a total data movement of Psi elements (for a data with Psi elements) for each. Therefore, the standard DP incurs 2Psi data movement during each training step.

claim: ZeRO stages 1 and 2 (optimizer-state and gradient partitioning) keep communication volume exactly equal to baseline DP at 2Psi.
stance_target: the claim that sharding optimizer states and gradients is communication-free relative to DDP
quoted_support: So the total communication volume per training step is Psi + Psi = 2Psi, exactly the same as the baseline DP.

claim: ZeRO stage 3 (parameter partitioning) raises total communication volume to 3Psi, i.e. 1.5x baseline DP.
stance_target: the 1.5x FSDP/ZeRO-3 vs DDP multiplier, corroborating the PyTorch FSDP paper's identical statement
scope_conditions: Pos+g+p; parameter all-gather in forward and again in backward, plus gradient reduce-scatter
quoted_support: The total volume is therefore 3Psi which is 1.5x compared to the baseline.

claim: A 7.5B-parameter model needs 120 GB of model-state memory under standard DP, 31.4 GB with optimizer-state partitioning at Nd=64, 16.6 GB with gradient partitioning added, and 1.88 GB with full parameter partitioning.
stance_target: the per-card memory budget arithmetic for a 7B-class model, directly relevant to whether 7B-total fits DDP on 64 GB cards
quoted_support: a 7.5 B parameter model requires 31.4GB of memory using Pos with 64-way DP (Nd = 64), while requiring 120 GB with standard DP ... a 7.5 B parameter model requires only 16.6 GB of memory using Pos+g with 64-way DP ... a 7.5 B parameter model requires 1.9 GB of model-state memory using Pos+p+g with 64-way DP.

claim: Without ZeRO, plain data parallelism can only train models below about 1.5 billion parameters on 32 GB devices.
stance_target: the claim that DDP's model-size ceiling is set by per-card capacity, so a 7B-total model on 64 GB cards is near or past the DDP limit
quoted_support: Without ZeRO, the largest model DP alone can run has less than 1.5 Billion parameters.

claim: ZeRO-3 with Nd=1024 can fit a one-trillion-parameter model, and with Nd=64 fits 128B parameters.
stance_target: the scaling headroom of full sharding versus the 5-GPU box's Nd=5
quoted_support: Note that, with Nd = 64, ZeRO can train models with up to 7.5B, 14B, and 128B parameters using Pos, Pos+g, and Pos+g+p, respectively. When Nd = 1024, ZeRO with all of its optimizations enabled (Pos+g+p) could train models with 1 Trillion parameters!

claim: ZeRO-100B sustained 15 PFLOPs (over 30% of peak) on 400 V100 GPUs, training models up to 170B parameters with 8x model size and 10x performance over Megatron-LM.
stance_target: the achievable MFU band (~30%) for data-parallel-style training at scale, a reference for the box's realistic throughput
scope_conditions: 400 V100 GPUs (25 DGX-2 nodes), 800 Gbps inter-node, GPT-2-like models 8B-170B
quoted_support: ZeRO-100B achieves a sustained throughput of 15 PetaFlops (over 30% of the peak) on average for models with 8B to 100B parameters.

claim: Model parallelism degrades sharply when it crosses a node boundary: per-link bandwidth drops from 300 GB/s on NVSwitch to 12.5 GB/s on InfiniBand EDR.
stance_target: the claim that TP/EP are ruled out on a fabric without a fast intra-node tier, since a PCIe Gen2 x4 link is far below even the 12.5 GB/s inter-node figure
scope_conditions: DGX-2 NVSwitch intra-node vs InfiniBand EDR inter-node
quoted_support: MP incurs high communication volume between GPUs, and going beyond a single node to fit larger models causes a communication bandwidth drop from 300GB/sec per link (NVSwitch) to 12.5 GB/sec per link (Infiniband EDR), resulting in a significant performance drop.

claim: ZeRO deliberately avoids CPU offload because PCIe bandwidth is severely constrained, noting that up to 50% of training time can be spent on GPU-CPU-GPU transfers.
stance_target: the claim that host-staged traffic over PCIe is the dominant penalty on this box, and that offloading model states to host RAM is not a free way to escape the 64 GB limit
scope_conditions: CPU offload of model states over PCIe
quoted_support: ZeRO differs in that it reduces the memory consumption significantly without storing the model states to CPU memory whose bandwidth is severely constrained due to PCI-E. ... Up to 50% of training time can be spent on GPU-CPU-GPU transfers.
numbers: up to 50% of training time on GPU-CPU-GPU transfers

claim: Activation memory dominates at long sequence lengths: a 100B model with batch 32, sequence length 1024 and MP degree 16 needs about 33 GB per GPU just for activation checkpoints, reducible to about 2 GB with partitioned activation checkpointing.
stance_target: the claim that 32k-context training is activation-bound, which is the premise behind CSA2's sparse-attention memory argument
scope_conditions: 100B model, batch 32, seq len 1024, MP degree 16, one checkpoint per transformer layer
quoted_support: If we checkpoint a single activation for each transformer layer, it would require about 33 GB of memory per GPU just to store the activation checkpoints. But with Pa in ZeRO, it can be reduced to about 2 GB

claim: Data-parallel communication volume is inversely proportional to batch size, so larger global batches amortize collective cost.
stance_target: the claim that a 1M-token global batch makes DDP's communication overhead relatively small on a slow fabric
quoted_support: The communication volume of a data-parallel training is inversely proportional to the batch

claim: ZeRO's super-linear speedup on 400 GPUs came with a 60B-parameter model at 38 TFLOPS per GPU.
stance_target: the per-GPU throughput reference for data-parallel training at scale
quoted_support: 38 TFlops per GPU, and aggregate performance over 15 Petaflops.
